To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PSA and PSA velocity are useful for prostate cancer detection.
the PSA test is not a perfect test for prostate cancer.
The sensitivity of PSA testing for prostate cancer is 60% in men aged <60 years, 70% in men aged 60–69 years, 80% in men aged >70 years and 90% in men aged ≥80 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) The performance of PSA in detecting prostate cancer in men aged 50–75 years, (2) PSA and its variants as a screening test for prostate cancer, (3) PSA and its derivatives as a marker for prostate cancer in men with a previous history of prostatic disease, (4) PSA and its performance in the detection of prostate cancer in men younger than age 50, (5) PSA and its role in the diagnosis of prostate cancer in the elderly, and
PSA testing and prostatism in young men, the role of PSA velocity in detecting prostate cancer, and the role of PSA testing in the diagnosis of prostate cancer in men with an elevated PSA.

PSA is a useful marker for prostate cancer, but that it is not specific enough for the detection of clinically significant disease.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PSA level is a useful marker, but that its value is enhanced by the addition of PSA velocity, PSA density and PSA doubling time.
the PSA test is not perfect and that the use of the PSA velocity is a more accurate way of assessing risk of prostatic cancer.
the use of PSA testing is a good way to detect prostate cancer, and that PSA velocity and PSA density are useful adjuncts to this.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PSA is a poor marker of cancer, but that it is a very good marker of prostatic cancer, and that the best way to use it is to use it with the knowledge that it is not a perfect marker.
the PSA velocity (rate of rise of serum PSA) is a more powerful marker of prostate cancer than is PSA itself.
PSA testing is best used as a screening test, and that the use of PSA velocity is a useful adjunct to PSA testing, particularly in men aged 60 years and older.
